title: Developer habit playbook: lightweight SDK paths (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a different angle on SDK onboarding: treat adoption as a set of small, repeatable developer habits rather than a single tutorial. The goal is to design a tiny set of friction-free rituals that nudge first-time users from curiosity to trusted integration in ~2 hours.

Audience:
- Engineers evaluating SDKs for a prototype (frontend, backend, mobile)
- Dev platform teammates who ship sample apps and troubleshooting flows
- Solutions engineers and early CS contacts running rapid proofs-of-concept

What is a "habit" in this context?
Short, observable action with immediate feedback. Examples we want to enable:
- "Hello token" — obtain API key and make a single successful call that returns a token count and latency measurement.
- "Sandbox prompt" — run a preseeded prompt that demonstrates streaming + function calling with a one-line change to the prompt template.
- "Embed-check" — generate an embedding and run a fuzzy match against a 3-line in-memory corpus.

Design principles (quick checklist for any path):
- Minimal cognitive load: 3 steps max to visible success.
- Immediate measurables: latency, token usage, returned shape.
- Reusable artifacts: code snippet should be copy-paste runnable in <60s.
- Failure-first visibility: error messages surfaced as actionable next steps.
- Portable: same snippet works in hosted & dedicated with a single config switch.

Lightweight paths (each path mapped to a 30–90 minute habit):
1) Rapid validation (30 min) — "Hello token"
   - Outcome: confirm credentials, region routing, and a generation response.
   - Steps: set API_KEY env var -> run sample (curl / node) -> inspect headers for x-token-cost / x-latency -> change model param and re-run.
   - Quick checks: HTTP 200, tokens_total > 0, latency < team SLO (150ms for quick path).

2) Interactive prompt loop (45 min) — "Sandbox prompt"
   - Outcome: show streaming and function/tool call wiring with stateful turn-taking.
   - Steps: open playground snippet -> swap sample prompt -> observe partial outputs streaming — then modify a small function schema to return structured JSON.
   - Teaching point: how to define function signatures and how Redwood preserves tool call fallback.

3) Small retrieval flow (60-90 min) — "Embed-check"
   - Outcome: confirm embedding pipeline + basic semantic search in-memory.
   - Steps: run embed-script to index 6 short docs -> run query -> inspect cosine scores -> display best match and highlight tokens.
   - Pitfalls to call out: inconsistent normalization, vector dimension mismatch, rate limits during bulk index.

4) Safety/Rate sim (30-45 min) — "Throttle & fallback"
   - Outcome: simulate a burst and verify automatic fallback to a cheaper model and graceful error messages.
   - Steps: use local load script to send concurrent requests -> validate routing logs and response codes -> check console shows fallback event.

Artifacts to ship with each path (must exist as single-file, copy-paste runnable):
- README (2 paragraphs) with expected outputs and "next step" suggestions
- Example app (one file): node/py/curl variant (choose 1 per language)
- Debug checklist (3 items) + expected header/metric values
- Short test prompt set (3 examples) for quick regression check

Observation and feedback signals (how we judge whether a habit succeeded):
- Local metric: sample app returns expected output in <N attempts
- Console telemetry: user invoked quickstart, opened logs, toggled model param
- Post-setup survey: 1-question inline pulse ("Did you get a working call?")
- SE/CS signal: number of triaged requests within first 48h after user completes a path

Developer ritual calendar (recommended):
- Day 0 (15 min): set API key + run "Hello token" path
- Day 1 (45 min): run "Sandbox prompt" and modify function signature
- Day 3 (60 min): run "Embed-check" for a real snippet from product docs

Open questions / trade-offs (brainstorm):
- Single-language vs multi-language: do we ship multi-language quickstarts or pick 1 canonical language per path?
- Where to put "explainability" hooks: in sample apps or as separate diagnostic tooling?
- How invasive should telemetry be during quickstart? minimal by default, opt-in richer traces.

Short TODO (prioritized):
- [ ] Create one copy-paste runnable node example for Hello token (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Produce embed-check python script and small dataset (owner: Grace)
- [ ] Add a tiny console banner that surfaces "complete first quickstart" for new orgs (owner: Tomás)
- [ ] Draft UX microcopy for common error codes (owner: Aisha)

Notes for implementers (practical tips):
- Use environment variables for api_key/region and detect missing creds with clear message and link to key creation flow.
- Prefer SDK helper methods that emit both human-friendly output and a machine-consumable JSON blob for tests.
- Keep dependencies zero or minimal: examples should run with a single modern node / python interpreter and one small pip/npm package at most.

Example quick snippet (conceptual, include in repo as runnable file):
- Node (curl-equivalent): set API_KEY=... ; node hello-token.js
- hello-token.js prints: "ok", model, tokens_used, latency_ms

Feedback loop: capture notes from initial pilot (3 orgs) and iterate once we have:
- median time-to-success < 45 minutes
- < 3 support tickets for onboarding per org in first week

Appendix: sample error messages to pre-bake microcopy for
- 401 -> "Missing/invalid API key. Quick fix: export REDWOOD_API_KEY and retry. Link: /docs/keys"
- 429 -> "Burst detected. Try a lower concurrency or enable burst capacity in Dedicated settings."
- vector dim mismatch -> "Embed dim mismatch. Check the model and the index vector size. See embed troubleshooting."

This doc is intentionally a sketch: prefer small iterative experiments over a large unified quickstart. We want multiple narrow, testable habits that give users confidence and a path to production integration.

Unresolved: where to host the canonical habit artifacts (repo vs console snippets vs package samples). Recommend a single public repo with language folders and a tiny web UI that surfaces the three paths for a user's org after they create a key.

End of draft.
